beats.care: Fake job offers and trading tips target people your age. If it promises easy money, stop and check.
beats.what: In September, Hyderabad's cybercrime police arrested 35 people in nine states and returned 88.48 lakh rupees to victims.
beats.why: Social media, investment, trading and fake digital arrest scams are rising fast, and most target people online.

cards.body: Figures from Additional CP M. Srinivasulu: arrests included 9 for social media fraud, 7 for investment fraud, 6 for digital arrest and 5 for trading fraud. Police also took down 1,457 profiles and 2,603 ads promoting betting, gaming and fake investments.
Scammers pose as police or officials on a video call, claim you're under arrest, and demand money to clear your name. Real police never arrest anyone over a video call.
cards.title: what is a digital arrest scam?

cards.body: Report quickly; the faster you report, the better the chance of freezing the money. You can also file at cybercrime.gov.in.
cards.caption: National cybercrime helpline

cards.q: Have you got a scam message this month?

opts: Promising easy money or creating panic
Asking you to visit a police station
Offering free cricket tickets in person
cards.q: What's the common trick in most of these scams?
cards.why: Scammers rush you with greed or fear so you pay before you think.
